facts.text: The three example tool chains are an open-source core with in-house integration, a model-based engineering stack with heavy-machine physics, and an integrated commercial chain with a partner; lowest, middle and highest describe relative cost and integration posture, not dollar figures.
facts.quote: labels them lowest, middle and highest by relative cost and integration posture, not by dollar figures.

facts.text: The three tool-chain cost levels are relative because almost every commercial vendor is quote-only.
facts.quote: Because almost every commercial vendor is quote-only, the levels are relative.

facts.text: All three example tool chains are expert assessments built from tool entries, integration findings and compute figures.
facts.quote: All three are expert assessment built from the tool entries, the integration findings and the compute figures [Chapter 11].

facts.text: The lowest-cost chain uses CARLA, Isaac Sim or Gazebo for sensors and environments, Project Chrono for machine dynamics and Soil Contact Model (SCM) terrain, and Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2).
facts.quote: CARLA, Isaac Sim or Gazebo for sensors and environments; Project Chrono for machine dynamics and Soil Contact Model (SCM) terrain; Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2)

facts.text: The lowest-cost chain adds in-house scenario scripts or Scenic, J1939 emulation to ISO/TS 21815-2, and on-premises RTX graphics cards or spot cloud.
facts.quote: in-house scenario scripts or Scenic; J1939 emulation to ISO/TS 21815-2; on-premises RTX graphics cards or spot cloud.

facts.text: The lowest-cost chain can provide camera and lidar sensor-in-the-loop, articulated and tracked dynamics on deformable terrain, and scripted job-site scenarios, with full control of intellectual property.
facts.quote: It can do camera and lidar sensor-in-the-loop, articulated and tracked dynamics on deformable terrain and scripted job-site scenarios, with full control of intellectual property.

facts.text: Without major work, the lowest-cost chain cannot provide validated radar, physics-based ultrasonic, weather effects with correlation evidence, vendor support or tool-qualification evidence; the chain also depends on hiring scarce skills.
facts.quote: Without major work it cannot provide validated radar, physics-based ultrasonic, weather effects with correlation evidence, vendor support or tool-qualification evidence, and it depends on hiring scarce skills.

facts.text: The middle-cost chain uses MATLAB and Simulink with the Offroad Autonomy Library, RoadRunner, RoadRunner Scenario, Unreal and sensor toolboxes, plus Mevea or AGX Dynamics coupled through the Functional Mock-up Interface (FMI) for terrain, hydraulics and machine variants.
facts.quote: MATLAB and Simulink with the Offroad Autonomy Library, RoadRunner and RoadRunner Scenario, Unreal and the sensor toolboxes; Mevea or AGX Dynamics coupled through the Functional Mock-up Interface (FMI) for terrain, hydraulics and machine variants

facts.text: The middle-cost chain includes one externally validated sensor model packaged to the ASAM Open Simulation Interface (OSI) as a Functional Mock-up Unit (FMU), Speedgoat or NI for later hardware-in-the-loop testing, and cloud GPUs for batch runs.
facts.quote: one externally validated sensor model packaged to the ASAM Open Simulation Interface (OSI) as a Functional Mock-up Unit (FMU); Speedgoat or NI for later hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing; cloud graphics processors (GPUs) for batch runs.

facts.text: The middle-cost chain provides credible machine dynamics, explicit construction and mining workflows, camera and lidar sensing, and HIL with real electronic control units, but not broad validated multi-sensor weather physics or large-scale coverage-driven scenario management.
facts.quote: It gives credible machine dynamics, explicit construction and mining workflows, camera and lidar sensing and HIL with real electronic control units (ECUs), but not broad validated multi-sensor weather physics or large-scale coverage-driven scenario management

facts.text: Module prices for the middle-cost tool chain are not public.
The highest-cost chain uses a commercial validation platform, with examples including dSPACE AURELION with SIMPHERA, VEOS and SCALEXIO, Applied Intuition, Cognata, VTD or Foretellix.
facts.quote: a commercial validation platform (for example dSPACE AURELION with SIMPHERA, VEOS and SCALEXIO; Applied Intuition; Cognata; VTD; or Foretellix)

facts.text: The highest-cost chain adds heavy-machine dynamics from IPG TruckMaker, Mevea, AGX or Vortex, specialist sensor simulation from AURELION or AVxcelerate, dSPACE or NI benches, and cloud execution.
facts.quote: heavy-machine dynamics from IPG TruckMaker, Mevea, AGX or Vortex; specialist sensor simulation (AURELION or AVxcelerate); dSPACE or NI benches; cloud execution

facts.text: The highest-cost chain includes an engineering partner such as AVL, IPG or Fraunhofer for integration and correlation.
facts.quote: an engineering partner such as AVL, IPG or Fraunhofer for integration and correlation.

facts.text: The highest-cost chain offers physics-based simulation of all four sensor types, large-scale regression and partner capacity for the four-month window.
facts.quote: It offers physics-based simulation of all four sensor types, large-scale regression and partner capacity for the four-month window

facts.text: The highest-cost chain cannot guarantee off-road sensor realism, avoid multi-vendor dependence or remove the manufacturer's own physical correlation tests.
facts.quote: but cannot guarantee off-road sensor realism, avoid multi-vendor dependence or remove the manufacturer's own physical correlation tests.

facts.text: No public evidence shows the highest-cost integrated commercial tool chain validated end to end for off-road automatic braking.
facts.quote: No public evidence shows this chain validated end to end for off-road automatic braking.

facts.text: At every tool-chain cost level, the recommended fourth architecture avoids making one simulator carry every test: use fast functional tests for millions of logic combinations, medium-fidelity dynamics for broad regression, high-fidelity rendering and soil only for sensitive subsets, HIL for timing, and targeted physical tests for correlation.
facts.quote: Use fast functional tests for millions of logic combinations, medium-fidelity dynamics for broad regression, high-fidelity rendering and soil only for sensitive subsets, HIL for timing, and targeted physical tests for correlation

facts.text: Allocation of tests across the multi-simulator architecture should be decided by sensitivity and correlation work, not assumption.
facts.quote: with the allocation decided by sensitivity and correlation work, not assumption [Chapter 11].
